goal: Design, implement, and verify a compact Alibaba Qwen3.8 Provider leaf contract, adaptive reasoning/output budgets, incremental repair feedback, and resume the preserved acceptance checkpoint.
acceptance_criteria: Alibaba Model Studio qwen3.8 Responses generation payloads explicitly use reasoning effort none, while other providers and models retain their existing payloads.

Qualified Qwen component-file calls receive a deterministic compact request containing the target, direct interfaces, applicable contracts, bounded invariants/context, newest repair delta, implementation budget, and exact response shape while broad project state remains local.

Representative simple, dependency-aware, and oversized leaf fixtures prove material prompt reduction, a hard effective-request character ceiling, dynamic output budgets, and secret-free request-profile telemetry.
Provider responses continue through the unchanged local output, interface, implementation-depth, checkpoint, post-build, packaging, and delivery validators.
Provider transport and kernel-contract tests cover the scoped reasoning policy and the reviewed Provider route remains unchanged.
The bounded diagnostic probe keeps its existing 128-Token and reasoning-none behavior without credential disclosure.
The preserved identity-bound Qwen acceptance checkpoint is resumed through cgkn_generate and any complete candidate is tested through cgkn_test_generated.

prevention: Confirm acceptance, interfaces, and applicable kernel constraints before implementation.
assurance: Review method, schema, skill, and repository instruction consistency.
Validate that support artifacts cannot authorize formal delivery PASS.
Review changed files against the kernel contract before integration.
control: Run targeted kernel and knowledge tests.
improvement: Record review findings and one bounded improvement experiment.

feedback: Compact Qwen leaf generation and hard-budget regression evidence passed; live delivery remained NOT_EVALUATED because Alibaba transport instability and the 900-second command limit prevented a complete candidate.

worked: Local-first contract compilation reduced ordinary live leaf requests by 76.6 percent while retaining Provider authorship and unchanged validation.
did_not_work: The live acceptance run was dominated by unstable TLS transport and repeated legacy post-build file-repair fallbacks, then timed out without a generation result.
experiments: Create a separate governed increment for compact post-build repair envelopes and clean identity-bound acceptance runs before spending more Provider quota.
